assignment.title: Algebra II Honors — Lesson 1: Transformations → Absolute Value Functions
assignment.essentialQuestion: How can transformations and key attributes be used to graph, analyze, and describe absolute value functions?
assignment.teacherNotes: Instructional sequence intentionally begins with general transformation language in an ALEKS-like graph-mapping progression, then narrows to absolute value. Reinforce the class rule “x’s lie; y’s tell the truth”: inside/x changes use opposite signs and reciprocal scale factors; outside/y changes act exactly as written. Require students to move defining points before connecting the transformed graph.

sections.title: Warm-Up — X's Lie, Y's Tell the Truth

questions.prompt: For g(x)=f(x−4)+3, describe the horizontal and vertical translations.

optionRationales.right 4: Inside f, x's lie: x − 4 moves every point 4 units right.
optionRationales.left 4: This reads the sign inside f at face value; x's lie, so a change inside f works opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The −4 sits inside f with x, so it does move the graph sideways.

optionRationales.up 3: The +3 is outside f, and y's tell the truth: every point moves up 3.
optionRationales.down 3: This reverses a change made outside f; y's tell the truth, so only changes inside f work in reverse.
optionRationales.none: The +3 is added to the output f(x), so it does move the graph vertically.

questions.prompt: Use the class rule “x's lie, y's tell the truth.” Describe g(x)=f(−2x).

optionRationales.across the y-axis: The negative is inside f, with x, so every point flips left to right across the y-axis.
optionRationales.across the x-axis: An x-axis reflection needs a negative outside f, like −f(x); this negative is inside, with x.
optionRationales.none: The −2 inside f carries a negative sign, and a negative with x is a reflection.

optionRationales.compression by 1/2: x's lie: the 2 inside f squeezes the graph toward the y-axis, to 1/2 its width.
optionRationales.stretch by 2: This reads the factor inside f at face value; x's lie, so a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 2 multiplies x inside f, so the width does change.

questions.prompt: Use the class rule “x's lie, y's tell the truth.” Describe g(x)=−(1/2)f(x)+2.

optionRationales.across the x-axis: The negative is outside f, so it flips every output: a reflection across the x-axis.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A y-axis reflection needs the negative inside f, with x, as in f(−x); this one multiplies the output.
optionRationales.none: The −1/2 in front of f carries a negative sign, and a negative output is a reflection.

optionRationales.compression by 1/2: y's tell the truth: multiplying every output by 1/2 squeezes the graph to half its height.
optionRationales.stretch by 2: This treats a factor outside f like one inside; y's tell the truth, so only a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 1/2 multiplies every output, so the height does change.

optionRationales.up 2: The +2 is outside f, and y's tell the truth: every point moves up 2.
optionRationales.down 2: This reverses a change made outside f; y's tell the truth, so only changes inside f work in reverse.
optionRationales.none: The +2 is added after f, so it does move the graph vertically.

questions.prompt: A graph of y=f(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=f(−x) by transforming each defining point.
A graph of y=g(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=−g(x) by transforming each defining point.
Below is the graph of y=−x³. Translate it to make the graph of y=−(x+3)³+2.
A graph of y=f(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=(1/2)f(x).
A graph of y=g(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=g((1/2)x). Remember: x-scale factors are reciprocal.
For g(x)=2f(−(1/2)(x−3))+4, describe every transformation from y=f(x).

optionRationales.across the y-axis: The negative in −(1/2) is inside f, with x, so the graph flips across the y-axis.
optionRationales.across the x-axis: The negative is inside f, with x; an x-axis reflection would need a negative in front of f.
optionRationales.none: The factor inside f is −1/2, and its negative sign is a reflection.

optionRationales.stretch by 2: x's lie: a factor of 1/2 inside f widens the graph, a horizontal stretch by 2.
optionRationales.compression by 1/2: This reads the factor inside f at face value; x's lie, so a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 1/2 multiplies the input inside f, so the width does change.

optionRationales.right 3: Inside f, x − 3 moves every point 3 units right.
optionRationales.left 3: This reads the sign inside f at face value; x's lie, so a change inside f works opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The −3 sits inside f with x, so the graph does move sideways.

optionRationales.stretch by 2: The 2 in front of f multiplies every output, so the graph stretches vertically by 2.
optionRationales.compression by 1/2: This treats a factor outside f like one inside; y's tell the truth, so only a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 2 in front of f multiplies every output, so the height does change.

optionRationales.none: The factor in front of f is a positive 2, so the outputs keep their signs: no vertical reflection.
optionRationales.across the x-axis: The only negative here is inside f, with x; a vertical reflection needs a negative in front of f.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A flip across the y-axis is horizontal; a vertical reflection comes only from a negative in front of f.

optionRationales.up 4: The +4 is outside f, and y's tell the truth: every point moves up 4.
optionRationales.down 4: This reverses a change made outside f; y's tell the truth, so only changes inside f work in reverse.
optionRationales.none: The +4 is added after f, so the graph does move vertically.

questions.prompt: Read y=−|x−2|+3 using “x's lie, y's tell the truth.” Describe the transformations of the absolute value parent function.

sections.title: Independent Practice — Narrow to Absolute Value

questions.prompt: The graph of y=g(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=−g(x)+3.
The graph of y=h(x) is shown. Draw the graph of y=2h(x+1).
For the absolute value parent function f(x)=|x|, identify its vertex, domain, and range.

optionRationales.(0, 0): |x| is smallest at x = 0, where |0| = 0, so the V turns at the origin.
optionRationales.(1, 0): (1, 0) would be the vertex of |x − 1|; the parent function is not shifted.
optionRationales.(0, 1): (0, 1) would be the vertex of |x| + 1; the parent function is not shifted.

optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): Any real number has an absolute value, so every x is allowed.
optionRationales.[0, ∞): This is the set of outputs; negative inputs are allowed too, since |−3| = 3.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): Every x can go into |x|, including 0 and negative numbers.

optionRationales.[0, ∞): An absolute value is never negative, and |0| = 0, so the outputs start at 0 and go up.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): This is the domain; the outputs of |x| are never negative.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): The output 0 does occur, at x = 0, so the range includes 0.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Can |x| ever be negative?

questions.prompt: Below is the graph of y=|x|. Translate it to make the graph of y=|x+2|−4.
Graph y=−|x−2|+3 by transforming the key points of y=|x|. Plot the transformed defining points first.
For y=|2x|−4, describe the horizontal dilation/compression and vertical translation shown by the written equation.

optionRationales.compression by 1/2: x's lie: the 2 multiplying x inside the bars makes the V narrower, a compression by 1/2.
optionRationales.stretch by 2: This reads the 2 inside the bars at face value; x's lie, so a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 2 multiplies x inside the bars, so the width does change.

optionRationales.down 4: The −4 is outside the bars, and y's tell the truth: every point moves down 4.
optionRationales.up 4: This reverses a change made outside the bars; y's tell the truth, so only changes with x work in reverse.
optionRationales.none: The −4 is subtracted after the absolute value, so the graph does move vertically.

optionRationales.(0, −4): |2x| is 0 at x = 0, and the −4 outside the bars moves that point down to (0, −4).
optionRationales.(−4, 0): The −4 is outside the bars, so it changes y, not x.
optionRationales.(0, 4): This reverses the −4; a change outside the bars keeps its sign.

questions.prompt: Adjust the transformation until your absolute value graph matches y=|2x|−4. Equivalent parameterizations that produce the same graph are accepted.
For $p(x)=|x|$, the domain is restricted to $-{{a}}\le x\le {{b}}$. What is the maximum value of $p$ on this interval?
supportHints: Identify how the function behaves on the stated inputs, then use that behavior to determine the maximum.

solutionReview.headline: Analyze the nonlinear function.
reasoning: For p(x)=|x| on a closed interval, compare the absolute values of the two endpoints.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The maximum is the larger of the two endpoint absolute values.

questions.prompt: Analyze y=−2|x+3|+1.

optionRationales.(−3, 1): |x + 3| is 0 at x = −3, and the +1 outside the bars puts that point at y = 1.
optionRationales.(3, 1): This reads the +3 inside the bars at face value; x's lie, so x + 3 moves the vertex the other way.
optionRationales.(−3, −1): This changes the sign of the +1, which is outside the bars; the −2 flips the V but does not move its vertex.

optionRationales.across the x-axis: The negative in −2 is in front of the bars, so it flips the outputs: the V opens down.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A y-axis reflection needs a negative inside the bars, with x; this negative multiplies the output.
optionRationales.none: The factor in front of the bars is −2, and its negative sign is a reflection.

optionRationales.stretch by 2: The 2 in −2 multiplies every output, so the V is twice as steep: a vertical stretch by 2.
optionRationales.compression by 1/2: This treats a factor outside f like one inside; y's tell the truth, so only a factor with x works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The −2 multiplies every output, so the steepness does change; its sign adds a reflection.

optionRationales.left 3: Inside the bars, x + 3 moves every point 3 units left.
optionRationales.right 3: This reads the +3 inside the bars at face value; x's lie, so the shift goes opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The +3 sits inside the bars with x, so the graph does move sideways.

optionRationales.up 1: The +1 is outside the bars, and y's tell the truth: every point moves up 1.
optionRationales.down 1: This reverses a change made outside the bars; y's tell the truth, so only changes with x work in reverse.
optionRationales.none: The +1 is added after the absolute value, so the graph does move vertically.

optionRationales.(−∞, 1]: The V opens down from its vertex at y = 1, so the outputs are 1 and everything below it.
optionRationales.[1, ∞): This is the range of a V that opens up; the negative in front of the bars makes this one open down.
optionRationales.(−∞, −1]: This changes the sign of the +1, which is outside the bars and keeps its sign.
